Shorter Agendas, More Decisions
Many managers assume a longer agenda saves time. In practice, the opposite happens. A typical agenda lists twelve items, and only the first and second receive full discussion. --(143)-- items, squeezed into the closing minutes, are carried over to the following week.
Preparation goes into filling the agenda --(144)-- settling the questions each item raises, so discussion runs out before agreement does. To change this, limit the next agenda to three decisions. A meeting built this way should --(145)-- more decisions in less time.
Not every meeting calls for this approach. Annual planning sessions only share information, so a long agenda suits them. --(146)--. Try it at your next meeting, and find more advice in Torrington Business Monthly.

Rating: 5 out of 5 stars
Title: A florist that truly delivers
Posted by Paula Reinhardt on March 18
I ordered flowers from Meadowgate Florist for a retirement celebration at my company, and I could not be happier. This was my first time using them. Gemma Fowler, a colleague in my department, spoke highly of the shop after her own event, and her praise alone persuaded me to try it. It is not the nearest florist to my office, and their prices were fair rather than the cheapest, but I trusted her judgment.
Their site advises placing large orders a full week ahead, yet they arranged mine with only two days' notice. On the day, they delivered the arrangement to my other office across town at no extra charge, which saved me a long trip.
When I called to swap the lilies for roses at the last minute, the staff took it in stride. The shop was plainly busy that afternoon, but nothing seemed to trouble them. Every stem was fresh, and the colors were exactly what I had described over the phone.
I will certainly use Meadowgate again. My colleagues kept asking where the flowers had come from, and I gladly gave them the name. In fact, I have already saved their number to book flowers for next month's staff anniversary event.
Verified order. Most readers found this review helpful.

We would like to invite you to an introductory session at the clubhouse. During the session, our instructors will cover the basic strokes, launching, and safety checks on calm water, so no prior training is needed. The session lasts around two hours and ends with refreshments in the clubhouse.

We have noted the request you made on your form, and everything will be ready for you when you arrive at the clubhouse. Please bring suitable clothing and shoes that can get wet.

Interest this season has been remarkably strong, and each session can take only a small number of newcomers at a time. For that reason, we will confirm your place by telephone as soon as a suitable date has been arranged.

We look forward to seeing you on the water.

Warm regards,
Marion Whitlock
Membership Coordinator, Cranleigh Canoe Club

Lakeview Gifts — Service News
Posted August 1
Gift wrapping has been offered at our two stores for years. It can now be added to any order for delivery as well. For delivery orders, the charge is two dollars for each item wrapped, the same as in our stores. To mark the new service, we have also added two paper designs, bringing the choice to six.

Tell us what you think: a feedback form follows every wrapped order.

Valerie Musgrave

Calvin Lockhart
